patch.value: Delta read projections: --since <cursor> on list, search, context, and get returns only what changed plus tombstones

An agent that re-orients every few minutes pays full projection cost each time, even when nothing it cares about moved. pm events shipped the mutation-side stream, but read projections have no incremental form: there is no way to ask list, search, context, or get for the difference since a previously returned cursor. This feature adds a server-side delta: given an opaque cursor from a prior response, the command returns only rows whose projected content changed, plus explicit tombstones for rows that left the result set, plus an unchanged-count so the agent can prove completeness without receiving the unchanged rows. The cursor is query-bound in the same way pagination cursors already are, so a delta can never be silently applied across a changed filter.

list, search, context, and get accept --since <cursor> and return changed rows, tombstones for rows that left the set, and an unchanged count that makes the delta verifiable; The cursor is query-bound and opaque: applying it to a different filter, projection, or format fails with a typed error rather than returning a misleading delta; A delta response over an unchanged workspace costs asymptotically less than the full projection and the saving is asserted by the token-cost corpus gate; Deltas are derived from the same durable substrate as the mutation event stream, with no separate bookkeeping to fall out of sync; The SDK exposes the delta as a typed primitive so packages and MCP get it without reimplementation; Correctness is proven by property tests that replay arbitrary mutation interleavings and assert delta-then-apply equals full-read
Repeat orientation costs tokens proportional to change, not to workspace size
Re-orientation is the single most repeated agent operation. Charging full projection cost for an unchanged workspace is the largest avoidable token expense in a long-lived agent session.
Makes continuous agent operation affordable at any workspace size and gives the returning-agent story a concrete mechanism instead of a manual diff.
Every read surface can be asked what changed since last time, and answers in bounded tokens with verifiable completeness.
The mutation event stream and durable pagination cursors both shipped; the delta is now composable from existing primitives rather than new infrastructure.

author: harness:claude-code
message: Delta reads are the mechanism behind the returning-agent and million-item stories

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Measured the cost of re-orientation on the live tracker 2026-08-03, which is the case this feature exists to serve.

Over a six-hour window, 144 recorded history entries touched 9 distinct items. The surfaces available to a returning caller answer that question three different ways and none of them answers it well.

pm context, the command whose entire purpose is orientation, accepts no time window at all: the flag is rejected with exit 2. Its default projection is 8879 bytes and is recomputed in full whether or not anything moved.

pm list accepts updated-after and returns 0 rows for that window under its default lifecycle scope, because all 9 changed items are terminal. Raising the scope to all returns the 9. The receipt reports total 0 without disclosing that a filter removed the entire delta.

pm activity accepts from and returns the 144 entries, but as operations rather than items: it names ids and ops, so the caller must fold 144 rows back into 9 item states and then read each one.

So the delta is either unavailable, silently empty, or expressed in a unit the caller cannot act on, and the full projection is the only reliable path. That is the asymmetry this feature closes, and it is worth noting that the unchanged-count in the acceptance criteria is the part that makes the answer trustworthy: without it, a delta of zero rows is indistinguishable from the scoped-away zero measured here.
